chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubayda, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
The son of al-mula'ana (cursing) inherits one-third from his mother, and the remainder is for the Imam of the Muslims, because his responsibility (for the father's absence/divorce) is upon the Imam.

key_terms.ابْنُ الْمُلَاعَنَةِ: Son of al-mula'ana (child of a woman whose husband cursed her)

ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance share of a son of al-mula'ana according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the financial liability of the Imam in the specific case of *Mula'ana*, where the husband's curse implies a lack of proven paternity, thereby exempting the biological father from inheritance duties. Consequently, the mother receives one-third of the estate, while the remaining two-thirds revert to the Imam, who acts as the *Wali* (guardian) to cover the father's share. This ruling underscores the Imam's role in maintaining the financial integrity of the family unit when paternity is legally ambiguous.
